subject: The Papyrus · The country that grows a lot of wheat — and still imports the most
html:
Two true facts that seem to contradict

Egypt grows a serious amount of wheat: around 9 million tonnes a year. And yet Egypt is, in most years, the largest wheat importer on the planet. Both are true at once, and holding them together is the whole story. (Source: FAOSTAT; USDA FAS.)

Why a big grower is also the biggest buyer

The answer is simple arithmetic: more than 100 million people, most of them eating subsidised baladi bread every day, need far more wheat than the thin Nile-valley farmland can grow. So Egypt produces a lot and buys a lot — the gap between what the land yields and what the population eats is filled by ships from the Black Sea and beyond. That's why a bad harvest or a war half a world away lands, within weeks, on the price of bread in Cairo.

It's the same constraint every Papyrus keeps circling back to: a huge population on a sliver of green (remember — about 96% of Egypt is desert). Bread is where that geography becomes breakfast. “Egypt grows lots of wheat” and “Egypt imports the most wheat” aren't a contradiction to resolve; they're two halves of one number — demand minus supply — that a data person learns to always compute.
